messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, the most conspicuous “dominant” genetic trait is the allele that produces the typical tawny coat color. This allele is found in the melanocortin‑1 receptor (MC1R) gene, which controls melanin production in fur. When a lion inherits the dominant MC1R allele from either parent, it will express the normal tawny coat that characterizes the species. (Male lions also develop a mane, but that is a secondary sexual trait rather than a single dominant allele.)
